messages.author: feaba58d41c5a493
messages.subject: Re: Code analysis of designed experiments with distance data?
parts:
The unmarked package for R includes a modeling option for abundance
based on distance sampling (Royle, J. A., D. K. Dawson, and S. Bates
2004. Modeling abundance effects in distance sampling. Ecology 85, pp.
1591-1597.) I don't know if this is similar to Buckland et al 2009 but
I thought it worth mentioning.

http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/unmarked/index.html

Matt

messages.author: d718c6bb1db28db2
messages.subject: Re: Code analysis of designed experiments with distance data?
parts:
The Royle et al paper is more related to modelling spatial distance
sampling data (and assumes that distances are grouped into intervals).
There is also code in Distance (the DSM engine) that does something
similar (see Hedley, S.L. and Buckland, S.T. 2004. Spatial models for
line transect sampling. /Journal of Agricultural, Biological and
Environmental Statistics/ *9*, 181-199). We are currently working on
more sophisticated spatial methods for Distance, based on: Wood, S.N.,
Bravington, M.V. and Hedley, S.L. 2008. Soap film smoothing. JRSS Series B.

We don't currently have documented code for designed experiments in
distance sampling. We have a research student developing improved
methods (which don't need the two-stage approach of the 2009 paper and
which allow random effects), and hope to get these methods, together
with the methods of the 2009 paper, into Distance, given funding and the
availability of the right programmer ...

Steve Buckland
